Hi Sam and team,

Thanks again for the kickoff last week. Per our call, we'd like to run a compact implementation workshop to get your telemetry piping and core runbooks in place so SREs and on-call engineers have deterministic playbooks on day one of go‑live. Proposed details: 

- When: Wed, May 22 — 10:00–12:00 PT (2-hour working session with a 30m follow-up)
- Where: Zoom (calendar invite link below)
- Goal: Ship a minimal observability surface for the first phase — dashboards, tracing hooks in 3 services, an error taxonomy, and initial alert routing to PD
- Deliverables by EOD May 24: runbook draft, tracing snippets applied to staging, dashboard skeletons, MAP (mutual action plan)

Agenda (working format):
1) 15m — quick context & success criteria (Holloway)
2) 45m — tracing hook placements and code walkthrough (gateway, inference-router, model-runner)
3) 30m — alert taxonomy & routing (who owns which PD escalation)
4) 30m — runbook template + playthrough (DB failover, model OOMs, inference latency regressions)

Attached: vendor-security-checklist.pdf (Sam — you had asked for the security pack), I will also circulate our MAP and trace snippets ahead of the session.

Ask: please confirm meeting time and add the names of the engineers who will have code access to staging. If you need to shift the window, we can slide +/- one day.

Marissa

Marissa / Sam — adding a short technical checklist so the workshop is actionable. I've attached trace-hook-snippets.patch and runbook-template.md for hands‑on work. Please ask your platform engineer to provision a staging namespace with the following endpoints accessible over the VPN prior to the workshop: api-gateway, inference-router, model-runner (v1).

Minimal tracing and instrumentation plan (we will pair during the session):
- Place OpenTelemetry span start/finish in the API gateway request path (service=api-gateway) to capture client->edge latency.
- Add a parent span at inference-router where routing decisions happen (service=inference-router). Propagate trace-id in the x-trace-id header.
- Instrument model-runner around token generation and cache retrievals (service=model-runner). Capture token_count, model_variant, kv_cache_hit boolean.
- Tag spans with: user_tier (prod/staging), request_type (generation/embedding/rerank), model_name, seq_length.

Error taxonomy (proposal):
- OBS-1000: Input validation error (client)
- OBS-2000: Router misroute / 5xx from downstream
- OBS-3000: Model execution OOM / model runtime error
- OBS-4000: Latency regression (p99 > SLO)

Runbook highlights to cover in the workshop:
- OBS-3000: immediate rollback to warmer checkpoint + model-variant fallback; page ML lead and SRE
- OBS-4000: increase concurrency throttles, enable prefix caching for heavy queries, short-term autoscale

Attaching: trace-hook-snippets.patch, runbook-template.md.

Laura Bennett
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Observability handoff & implementation workshop — Holloway Health

Adding the ops & alerting perspective. See the attached observability-MAP-v1.xlsx — it's a one‑pager that ties alerts -> owners -> runbook entry -> PD service. A few recommendations ahead of the workshop: 

- PagerDuty mapping:
  - OBS-3000 (model OOMs) -> PD escalation to on-call ml-eng -> if ack > 15m escalate to infra SRE
  - OBS-4000 (latency p99) -> PD to infra SRE; thresholded by 3 consecutive 5m buckets

- Sampling & noise reduction: set trace sampling to 10% for production traces initially; 100% for errors. Apply adaptive sampling for heavy endpoints.

- Canary & rollout: we will create a canary route that sends 5% of traffic to the new instrumented binary so we can validate end-to-end without impacting prod. We'll coordinate with your release window (PG-3721).

- Dashboards: minimal dashboards we will build in the session -> 1) latency by model & route, 2) error breakdown by OBS code, 3) traffic & cache-hit rate.

Attaching: observability-MAP-v1.xlsx

Ben Carter
Customer Reliability Lead, Redwood Inference
